abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening, infection-triggered syndrome of dysregulated inflammation and immune dysfunction. However, the mechanisms underlying immune escape in sepsis remain poorly understood and merit further investigation. Gene expression data for sepsis were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database: GSE65682 was used to construct the training cohort, and GSE95233 served as an independent validation cohort. Feature genes were screened by integrating differential expression profiling with Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). A diagnostic model was developed and validated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, a nomogram, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network analyses were also performed. Finally, consensus clustering was applied to identify molecular subtypes of sepsis. Three feature genes were identified by differential expression analysis and WGCNA. Area under the curve (AUC)-based screening selected two diagnostic genes (NXT1 and UXS1), which demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (AUC > 0.9). Immune infiltration analysis revealed distinct patterns between the Sepsis and Control groups. Regulatory network analysis identified key miRNAs targeting these two genes and lncRNAs that regulate those miRNAs. Two sepsis subtypes with distinct immune and molecular characteristics were further identified. This study systematically explored the association between immune escape and the pathogenesis of sepsis and, through the integration of multiple bioinformatics approaches, elucidated the immune microenvironmental characteristics and molecular regulatory mechanisms of the disease, providing new insights into understanding its pathophysiology and developing targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study identifies NXT1 and UXS1 as novel diagnostic biomarkers for sepsis with high predictive accuracy (AUC > 0.9). By integrating differential expression analysis, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), and immune infiltration, we reveal distinct immune microenvironmental characteristics associated with sepsis pathogenesis. We further define two molecular subtypes of sepsis with heterogeneous immune profiles, providing new insights into immune dysfunction and immune escape in sepsis, which may facilitate the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

summary: Integrates GEO sepsis cohorts with WGCNA and differential expression to nominate NXT1 and UXS1 as diagnostic genes, plus ceRNA and immune infiltration analyses.
title: A novel immune-escape signature and classifier for predicting sepsis constructed by integrative bioinformatics.
